doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Growing up on R&B in Chicago while his father rehearsed at home
summary: Freeman says he loved R&B and sang in a group, went to school with Earth, Wind & Fire members, and heard his father rehearse with Pat Patrick, Clifford Jordan and others.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So I have this feeling in reading about you that it wasn’t just the saxophone or just jazz that you were interested in.
That’s true. I have a pretty varied background when it comes to music. I’ve been involved with different genres and types of music, because I like all genres and types.
When you grew up, I mean you obviously had the influence of your father, but there was certainly lots of pop music and so forth going on at the same time. Which of it caught your attention first?

Well naturally, like any kid, teenager, you grow up listening to the music that you grow up listening to, so I was no different. So at first it was R&B, rhythm & blues, all the singing groups, because I actually sang in a singing group. I had my own singing group. I sang in a few — did all the talent shows in high school. So I was listening to R&B, which would be Motown and the Drifters and things like that. Coming from Chicago, there was groups like the Impressions, Curtis Mayfield, Jerry Butler, you know the Chicago groups that were there. And Chicago was pretty much a hotbed of talented artists. I mean Earth, Wind & Fire comes from there. I went to school with them in fact. Well I didn’t go to school with Maurice, he was older, but the Emotions, we were together in class, we were in the same class. And a lot of Maurice’s brothers, Freddy and Verdine. Because Maurice had some brothers that were involved with Earth, Wind & Fire. So I went to school with all of them. And it’s like I grew up listening to that. That’s where I started. Of course, at the same time I was listening to my father rehearse simultaneously in the house. So I was listening to people like Pat Patrick and Clifford Jordan and they’d come by the house and
they’d be rehearsing with my dad and his bands. Don Baldwin, Andrew Hill, Vernel Fournier.
